title: OLYMPIAD SCIENCE — Chemistry | Organometallic Chemistry
description: Subject-wise test on Organometallic Chemistry (Chemistry) for OLYMPIAD SCIENCE. 15Q.

questions.question: Which of the following organometallic reagents is primarily known for undergoing 1,4-addition (conjugate addition) to α,β-unsaturated carbonyl compounds, rather than direct 1,2-addition?

options.explanation: Grignard reagents (e.g., methylmagnesium bromide) are hard nucleophiles that typically favor 1,2-addition to the carbonyl carbon due to their high reactivity.
Organolithium reagents (e.g., phenyllithium) are highly reactive and generally undergo 1,2-addition to carbonyl compounds rather than 1,4-addition.
Lithium dimethylcuprate (Gilman reagent) is a soft nucleophile that selectively undergoes 1,4-addition (conjugate addition) with α,β-unsaturated carbonyl compounds.
Organozinc reagents (e.g., diethylzinc) are less reactive and may participate in 1,4-addition, but they are not as selective or commonly used for this purpose as lithium dimethylcuprate.

questions.explanation: Lithium dimethylcuprate (Gilman reagent) is a soft nucleophile that preferentially undergoes 1,4-addition (conjugate addition) with α,β-unsaturated carbonyl compounds due to its lower reactivity and better compatibility with the extended π-system of the substrate.
questions.hint: Consider the reactivity and selectivity of organometallic reagents towards α,β-unsaturated carbonyls.
questions.subject: olympiad-sci-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is NOT typically classified as an organometallic compound?

options.explanation: Methylmagnesium bromide (CH3MgBr) has a direct metal-carbon bond (C-Mg), making it an organometallic compound.
Ferrocene (Fe(η5-C5H5)2) contains iron-carbon bonds, classifying it as an organometallic compound.
Tetracarbonylnickel(0) (Ni(CO)4) has nickel-carbon bonds, making it an organometallic compound.
Sodium methoxide (CH3ONa) does not have a direct metal-carbon bond; the carbon is bonded to oxygen, not directly to sodium, so it is not classified as an organometallic compound.

questions.explanation: Organometallic compounds are defined as compounds containing at least one direct metal-carbon bond. Sodium methoxide (CH3ONa) does not have a direct metal-carbon bond; the carbon is bonded to oxygen, not directly to sodium.
questions.hint: Consider the definition of an organometallic compound and the nature of the bonds in each option.
questions.subject: olympiad-sci-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is NOT considered an organometallic compound?

options.explanation: Grignard reagents have a direct carbon-magnesium bond, making them organometallic.
Ferrocene has iron-carbon bonds to cyclopentadienyl rings, making it organometallic.
Sodium ethoxide contains a carbon-oxygen bond but no direct carbon-metal bond, so it is not organometallic.
Zeise's salt has a platinum-carbon bond via ethylene, making it organometallic.

questions.explanation: Organometallic compounds are characterized by a direct carbon-metal bond. Sodium ethoxide (CH3CH2ONa) contains a carbon-oxygen bond but no direct carbon-metal bond, making it an organometallic compound.
questions.hint: Look for the presence of a direct carbon-metal bond.
questions.subject: olympiad-sci-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following organometallic compounds is commonly used as a catalyst in the Ziegler-Natta polymerization of alkenes?

options.explanation: Ferrocene is a metallocene but not used in Ziegler-Natta polymerization.
This combination is the classic Ziegler-Natta catalyst for alkene polymerization.
Ni(CO)₄ is used in hydroformylation but not in Ziegler-Natta polymerization.
Grignard reagents are nucleophilic reagents but not catalysts for Ziegler-Natta polymerization.

questions.explanation: The Ziegler-Natta catalyst is a combination of TiCl₄ and Al(C₂H₅)₃, which facilitates the stereospecific polymerization of alkenes.
questions.hint: Consider catalysts used in industrial polymerization processes.
questions.subject: olympiad-sci-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 18-electron rule is correct?

options.text: It applies only to organometallic compounds of transition metals in their highest oxidation states.
options.explanation: The rule applies broadly to transition metal organometallics, not just highest oxidation states.

options.text: It states that stable organometallic compounds tend to have 18 valence electrons around the metal center.
options.explanation: This is the core statement of the 18-electron rule.

options.text: It is violated by all metallocenes.
options.explanation: Many metallocenes, like ferrocene, satisfy the 18-electron rule.

options.text: It is satisfied by all metal carbonyls regardless of the metal’s oxidation state.
options.explanation: Metal carbonyls may or may not satisfy the rule depending on the metal and its oxidation state.

questions.explanation: The 18-electron rule states that organometallic compounds are most stable when the metal center has 18 valence electrons, analogous to the noble gas configuration.
questions.hint: Recall the analogy to the noble gas electron configuration.
questions.subject: olympiad-sci-chemistry

questions.question: The bonding in ferrocene, Fe(C₅H₅)₂, can be best described as:

options.text: Ionic bonding between Fe²⁺ and two C₅H₅⁻ ions
options.explanation: While the cyclopentadienyl rings are often considered as C₅H₅⁻, the bonding is more accurately described as covalent with π-backbonding.

options.text: A purely σ-bonded structure with no π-interactions
options.explanation: Ferrocene involves significant π-backbonding between Fe and the cyclopentadienyl rings.

options.text: A sandwich structure with π-backbonding from Fe to the cyclopentadienyl rings
options.explanation: This accurately describes the bonding in ferrocene.

options.text: A linear arrangement with Fe bonded to two separate C₅H₅ radicals
options.explanation: Ferrocene has a sandwich structure, not a linear arrangement.

questions.explanation: Ferrocene has a sandwich structure where iron is bonded to two cyclopentadienyl anions via π-backbonding, contributing to its stability.
questions.hint: Consider the structure and bonding in metallocenes.
questions.subject: olympiad-sci-chemistry

questions.question: For the compound [PtCl₂(C₂H₄)], which of the following best describes the nature of the Pt–C₂H₄ bond?

options.text: A purely ionic bond between Pt²⁺ and C₂H₄
options.explanation: The bond is not purely ionic; it involves covalent interactions.

options.text: A coordinate covalent bond where C₂H₄ acts as a π-acceptor ligand
options.explanation: Ethylene acts as a π-acceptor ligand in this complex.

options.text: A triple bond between Pt and one carbon atom of ethylene
options.explanation: There is no triple bond; the bonding involves π-backdonation.

options.text: A hydrogen bond involving the H atoms of C₂H₄
options.explanation: The bond is not a hydrogen bond; it is a coordinate covalent bond.

questions.explanation: In [PtCl₂(C₂H₄)], ethylene acts as a π-acceptor ligand, forming a coordinate covalent bond with Pt through backdonation from Pt to the π* orbital of C₂H₄.
questions.hint: Consider the role of ethylene as a ligand in organometallic chemistry.
questions.subject: olympiad-sci-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following organometallic compounds is most likely to undergo β-hydride elimination?

options.explanation: Ti(CH₃)₄ has no β-hydrogens, so it cannot undergo β-hydride elimination.
This compound has β-hydrogens and is prone to β-hydride elimination.
W(CO)₆ is a metal carbonyl and does not undergo β-hydride elimination.
Cr(C₆H₆)₂ is a metallocene and does not undergo β-hydride elimination.

questions.explanation: β-hydride elimination is common in alkyl complexes where the alkyl group has β-hydrogens. Ni(CH₂CH₃)₂ has β-hydrogens and can undergo this reaction.
questions.hint: Recall that β-hydride elimination requires β-hydrogens in the alkyl group.

questions.question: The reaction of a Grignard reagent (RMgX) with a ketone (R'₂CO) typically yields:

options.explanation: Grignard reagents do not typically yield carboxylic acids with ketones.
The reaction of a Grignard reagent with a ketone followed by hydrolysis yields a tertiary alcohol.
Grignard reagents do not yield aldehydes when reacting with ketones.
Esters are not the typical product of Grignard reagents reacting with ketones.

questions.explanation: Grignard reagents react with ketones to form tertiary alcohols after hydrolysis, as the nucleophilic R⁻ adds to the carbonyl carbon.
questions.hint: Consider the nucleophilic addition of Grignard reagents to carbonyl compounds.
questions.subject: olympiad-sci-chemistry

questions.question: In the compound (CH₃)₂PtCl₂, the oxidation state of platinum is:

options.explanation: Platinum is not in the zero oxidation state in this compound.
The oxidation state of Pt is +2 in (CH₃)₂PtCl₂.
The oxidation state is not +4; the calculation shows it is +2.
The oxidation state of Pt is not negative in this compound.

questions.explanation: Chlorine has an oxidation state of -1, and there are two Cl atoms. The two methyl groups are neutral ligands. Therefore, Pt must be +2 to balance the charge: 2(-1) + Pt = 0 → Pt = +2.
questions.hint: Use the oxidation state rules for ligands and the overall charge of the compound.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of metallocenes?

options.text: They contain only σ-bonds between the metal and the ligands.
options.explanation: Metallocenes involve π-bonding, not just σ-bonds.

options.text: They have a sandwich structure with parallel cyclopentadienyl rings.
options.explanation: This is a defining feature of metallocenes.

options.text: They are always paramagnetic due to unpaired electrons.
options.explanation: Many metallocenes, like ferrocene, are diamagnetic.

options.text: They cannot undergo electrophilic substitution reactions.
options.explanation: Metallocenes, such as ferrocene, can undergo electrophilic substitution reactions.

questions.explanation: Metallocenes, such as ferrocene, exhibit a sandwich structure where the metal is sandwiched between two parallel cyclopentadienyl rings.
questions.hint: Consider the structural features of metallocenes.

questions.question: The compound V(CO)₆ is unstable at room temperature and readily dimerizes. This instability is primarily due to:

options.text: Steric hindrance between the CO ligands
options.explanation: Steric hindrance is not the primary reason for instability in V(CO)₆.

options.text: The 17-electron configuration of V(CO)₆, making it an odd-electron species
options.explanation: The 17-electron configuration makes V(CO)₆ unstable and prone to dimerization.
Electronegativity of vanadium is not the primary factor in this instability.

options.text: The inability of CO to act as a π-acceptor ligand
options.explanation: CO is a strong π-acceptor ligand, which is not the issue here.

questions.explanation: V(CO)₆ has 17 valence electrons (V contributes 5, each CO contributes 2), making it an odd-electron species prone to dimerization to achieve stability.
questions.hint: Consider the electron count and stability of organometallic compounds.

questions.question: Which of the following organometallic compounds is used in the Monsanto process for acetic acid production?

options.explanation: Wilkinson’s catalyst is used in hydrogenation, not the Monsanto process.
This iridium complex is the catalyst used in the Monsanto process.
The Ziegler-Natta catalyst is used in polymerization, not the Monsanto process.
Grubbs catalyst is used in olefin metathesis, not the Monsanto process.

questions.explanation: The Monsanto process uses an iridium complex, [Ir(CO)₂I₂]⁻, as the catalyst for the carbonylation of methanol to produce acetic acid.
questions.hint: Recall the industrial processes involving organometallic catalysts.

questions.question: Consider the following reaction sequence: CH₃CH₂COOCH₃ (methyl propanoate) reacts with excess CH₃MgBr followed by H₃O⁺. What is the major product X?

options.explanation: Correct. The reaction of methyl propanoate with excess CH₃MgBr followed by H₃O⁺ yields 2-methylbutan-2-ol as the major product.
Incorrect. 2-butanol is a secondary alcohol, which cannot be formed from this reaction sequence.
Incorrect. 3-methylbutan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol and does not match the product of this reaction.
Incorrect. This product would require a different starting material or reaction pathway.

questions.explanation: Esters react with two equivalents of a Grignard reagent to form a tertiary alcohol. The first equivalent of CH₃MgBr converts the ester to a ketone intermediate, and the second equivalent adds to the ketone to form a tertiary alcohol. The product is 2-methylbutan-2-ol.
questions.hint: Recall that esters react with two equivalents of Grignard reagents to form tertiary alcohols.

questions.question: Upon heating, the complex [CpCo(CO)2] (where Cp = η5-C5H5) undergoes dimerization to form a stable dinuclear complex. Assuming the dimerization occurs via loss of CO ligands and formation of metal-metal bonds, which of the following is the most plausible structure for the dimer, satisfying the 18-electron rule for each metal center?

options.explanation: This structure satisfies the 18-electron rule for each Co center with two bridging CO ligands and a Co-Co bond.
This structure does not account for the loss of CO ligands or the formation of metal-metal bonds, and the electron count would not satisfy the 18-electron rule.
This structure has only one bridging CO ligand, which is insufficient to satisfy the 18-electron rule for both Co centers.
This structure retains all CO ligands, which does not account for the dimerization process involving loss of CO ligands.

questions.explanation: The monomer [CpCo(CO)2] has an electron count of 18 (Cp contributes 5 electrons, Co contributes 9, and two CO ligands contribute 4 electrons). Upon dimerization, two CO ligands are lost to form metal-metal bonds, reducing the electron count per metal center. The structure must satisfy the 18-electron rule for each Co center. (CpCo)2(μ-CO)2 has two bridging CO ligands, each contributing 2 electrons to both metals, satisfying the 18-electron rule for each Co center.
questions.hint: Consider the 18-electron rule and the role of bridging ligands in stabilizing the dimer.
